q1.directions: Use the passage below to answer all parts of the question that follows.

parts.a: Describe ONE way in which the internet has increased global economic integration.
parts.b: Explain ONE reason why the spread of the internet has been uneven across the world, using the historian's interpretation in the passage.
parts.c: Explain ONE way in which digital technology has changed the nature of work in the twenty-first century.

sample_answers.a: The internet lets businesses coordinate production, sales, and services instantly across continents — a company can design in California, manufacture in Vietnam, and sell in Europe through a single digital network.
sample_answers.b: According to the passage, internet access depends on infrastructure, wealth, and education that are concentrated in developed countries and urban areas, so the poorest regions — lacking electricity, let alone broadband — remain excluded from the digital economy.
sample_answers.c: Digital platforms enabled remote work, the gig economy, and outsourcing of services (such as call centers and software development) to low-wage countries, detaching many jobs from fixed workplaces and national labor markets.

q1.stimulus:
Historians identify the internet as the defining technology of contemporary globalization — the infrastructure that made a truly integrated world economy possible. Beginning as an American military-academic network, the internet commercialized in the 1990s and spread with astonishing speed, connecting billions of people and allowing the instantaneous movement of capital, information, and services across borders. Yet historians also stress the 'digital divide': access remains deeply unequal, concentrated in wealthy countries and cities, while billions — especially in sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia — remain offline or barely connected. The internet thus simultaneously unites and divides: it creates a single global marketplace for those inside the network while marginalizing those outside it.
—Historian's account of technology and economic integration in the period c. 1900–present

q2.directions: Use the passage below to answer all parts of the question that follows.

parts.a: Identify ONE claim the author makes about the internet's economic significance.
parts.b: Describe ONE way in which the internet differs from earlier communications technologies in its economic impact.
parts.c: Explain ONE reason why governments have struggled to regulate the digital economy.

sample_answers.a: The author claims the internet is not merely a faster telephone but a new economic infrastructure that collapses the costs of coordination, making global supply chains and instant financial transactions possible.
sample_answers.b: Unlike the telegraph or telephone, which transmitted messages, the internet transmits the work itself — software, designs, financial instruments, services — so production no longer needs to happen where consumption does.
sample_answers.c: Digital businesses operate across borders instantaneously, outpacing national laws; regulators in one country cannot easily control companies headquartered elsewhere, and the technology evolves faster than legislation.

q2.stimulus:
The internet represents something genuinely new in economic history. Earlier technologies — the telegraph, the telephone, the fax — made it cheaper to communicate across distance. The internet makes it cheap to collaborate across distance. A programmer in Bangalore, a designer in Berlin, and a manager in Boston can now work on the same product simultaneously, as if seated at the same table. Capital moves at the speed of light; supply chains reorganize overnight. The constraint is no longer geography but connectivity — and billions remain on the wrong side of that divide.
—Adapted from an economist's account of the digital economy, early 2000s

q3.directions: Use the chart below to answer all parts of the question that follows.

parts.a: Describe ONE trend shown in the chart of internet users.
parts.b: Explain ONE cause of the rapid growth shown in the chart after 2000.
parts.c: Explain ONE economic consequence of the trend shown in the chart.

sample_answers.a: The chart shows the number of internet users worldwide rising from near zero in 1990 to billions by the 2020s, with the steepest growth after 2000 — one of the fastest technology adoptions in history.
sample_answers.b: The spread of affordable mobile phones (especially smartphones) brought internet access to developing countries without requiring expensive wired infrastructure, while falling costs and expanding networks made connection affordable for billions.
sample_answers.c: Billions of new users created vast new markets for e-commerce, digital services, and advertising, while also enabling outsourcing and remote work that integrated developing-country labor into the global economy.

q3.stimulus: The chart, from Our World in Data (Creative Commons BY license), shows the number of internet users worldwide from 1990 to the present. The curve rises slowly through the 1990s, then accelerates sharply after 2000, reaching billions of users — illustrating how the internet went from a niche academic network to a mass global infrastructure within a single generation.
